new_result.interpretation: Public CTBTO material establishes how deployed UWS calibration sequences are generated, that they are stored/processed at the IDC, and that H10S derived digitizer responses changed around the 2013 fault. The underlying calibration-sequence bytes were not recovered in this bounded pass. This is provenance recovery, not a preregistered causal test.

reasons.COUSTEAU_HA10_PRE_POST_2013_CROSSTALK_TR: The exact frozen 2013 EarthScope six-channel waveform gate already returned 240/240 HTTP 404 no-data requests. No access-condition change is known.
reasons.COUSTEAU_HA10_CALIBRATION_SEQUENCE_PUBLI: The council-selected bounded public recovery pass has just been completed. Repeating the same public search without a new source or custodian access path would not add independent evidence.

whole_picture_so_far.fact_1: CTBTO material documents an H10S1 electrical-noise event on 2013-07-19 that evolved into persistent noise with time-variable cross-talk into H10S2/H10S3; H10S1 was excluded from IDC Operations. Possible riser failure remains an interpretation, not a proven mechanism.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_2: The deployed UWS calibration sequence is a digitizer-electronics test: the relay excludes hydrophone ceramic, preamplifier and riser cable. The public presentation says calibration data are stored at the CTBTO IDC and processed from a known pseudo-random broadband calibration sequence plus other components.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_3: The same public CTBTO material reports H10S calibration-response changes around the fault era, including 0.8396 dB for H10S1 between March and September 2013 and two H10S2/H10S3 pair maxima of 4.7832 and 2.5340 dB in 1-100 Hz, while H10N 2013-vs-2017 changes are only thousandths of a dB.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_4: EarthScope public StationXML does not encode this 2013 fault-era calibration history: all six EDH channels expose one static 2004-open response epoch in the JANUS audit.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_5: The cleanest direct public waveform test across the 2013 fault is archive-blocked: 240/240 frozen EarthScope waveform requests returned no data although response metadata exist.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_6: JANUS 2014-2015 public waveforms repeatedly show an approximately 12-13 dB broadband H10S2-over-H10N1 excess. Public StationXML response correction changes the ratio only by tenths of a dB and therefore neither creates nor removes it.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_7: The published 2013 calibration-response deltas and the later 12-13 dB broadband cross-station power offset are different statistics and cannot be substituted as a one-to-one numerical explanation.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_8: A distinct pre-2013 literature thread reports repetitive H10 data-logger electronic noise causing spurious coherent zero-lag cross-correlations roughly during 2005-2009. Therefore PRE-2013 cannot automatically be treated as instrument-clean, and this older phenomenon must remain separate from the 2013 H10S1 fault unless bridged independently.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_9: December 2014 shows a persistent scale-like S2/N1 baseline; January strict per-window scalar generalization fails at two dayparts while central medians remain near that baseline, supporting persistent baseline plus episodic residuals rather than one exact scalar.
whole_picture_so_far.fact_10: The physical geometry lane remains independent. PDC/01236 bounding geometry contains H10N1 but not H10S2; exact native swath/track crossing and morphology at the frozen points remain open.
whole_picture_so_far.assistant_current_hypothesis: The strongest economical synthesis is a mixed superposition: persistent site/trunk/propagation/seabed or analogue-path baseline + an H10S measurement-chain problem not represented by public StationXML + episodic residual contamination. The available evidence does not yet partition their contributions.
whole_picture_so_far.strongest_countermodel: The large baseline could primarily be persistent site/path physics, while documented H10S electronics faults add only intermittent contamination. Conversely, an unmeasured analogue/riser contribution could dominate the baseline. Earliest simultaneous six-channel waveforms and independent native seabed geometry are the cleanest remaining discriminators.

available_next_discriminators.first_available_six_channel_baseline: Find the earliest public epoch where all six HA10 EDH waveforms are simultaneously available using availability metadata or bounded date discovery before inspecting waveform values; then freeze windows and compare six-channel baseline/coupling morphology against 2014-2015.
available_next_discriminators.native_bathymetry_swath_intersection: Establish exact native multibeam/backscatter/swath crossing and physical morphology at H10N1/H10S2 independently of hydrophone calibration.
available_next_discriminators.custodian_calibration_reply: Obtain authoritative IDC/CTBTO calibration sequence bytes, calibration-event table or raw historical waveforms through custodian response/access rather than repeated public search.

Respect the v3 progress guard: do not repeat the archive-blocked 2013 waveform gate or the just-completed calibration public-recovery pass without changed access/evidence. Prefer a new evidence axis, preserve the independent bathymetry lane, and veto all 119-Hz reinterpretation.
